value.rationale: The original expansion theorem suggests that sign reversal has nearly invariant periodic data. The new identity isolates precisely how each attracting odd-cycle orbit changes all odd period-dividing counts and the full zeta ratio. This is a structural dynamical invariant rather than a relabeling of the expanding proof. The constructive family demonstrates that relaxing expansion does not merely cause a small finite correction: the first-period discrepancy can be arbitrarily negative while branches remain real-analytic and strictly increasing. These facts can organize comparisons of nonuniform Lorenz maps and make the boundary of the expanding theorem explicit.
